note: Oxford is educational backstory; inherited estate is the earthly starting setting, without a stated geographical address.

Ancient enlarged house; library predates printing and occupies most ground floor. Large chief room nearly ceiling-high shelves, adjoining irregular rooms connected by doors, arches, short passages and up/down steps. Window overlooks central lawn fountain. August rain, evening sunset. Portrait niche in bookshelves; other portraits in gallery/great rooms.

Low narrow thick masked door with projecting frame and false book-backs; closet of rare old books has no other exit. Fixed mutilated parchment manuscript. Apparent disappearance through closet is observed but unexplained.
House haunting and an unnamed village are reported by butler via an old woman; Raven and Sir Upward disappear. Not proof of a second physical closet exit.

places: Vane house; Library; Hall; Garret; Mirror chamber
note: Route: library to hall, across to great staircase, first floor chief rooms, wide corridor, narrower stair to second floor, passages, door, winding wooden stair, main garret. Huge beams/rafters, long gloomy vistas, doors, few cobwebbed windows and small dusky skylights. Central rough unpainted plank enclosure with small dusty sunlit chamber and narrow dusty mirror, ebony frame, eagle, chain and ball.

Mirror ceases to reflect house. Near flat melancholy moor, middle low desolate strangely shaped heathy hills, far horizon mountain tops. Stone foreground; step over probable frame leads to open-air houseless heath. Depth sequence is explicit; compass direction absent.

Behind entry all vague as fog/field or cloud/mountainside; no familiar house or visible door. Ground and low plants with wind real to senses. No shining sun yet raven shadow. Narrator explicitly warns language and remembered forms cannot fully describe this world.

Raven says door out leads farther in; whereness and feeling at home determine orientation. Entry/exit not ordinary doors; Raven can travel between worlds. These are Raven's statements, not measured coordinates.

Loss of earthly name and identity; Raven transforms. Home described as the one place allowing passage both in and out; disappearance may be distance or heather cover. Narrator questions whether he is dead: conjecture, not confirmation.

places: Heath; Pine portal; Mirror chamber; Garret; Library
note: Follow Raven's direction then turn toward tall slender fragrant pine wood. Twilight interior; shimmer between two trunks like heat haze loses visibility close up, trees beyond uncertain. Shock and fall through it return to plank chamber and mirror. Descending spiral then repeated passages reaches great stair and library. No measured woodland distance or direction.
House seems threatening; imagined purchase of Swiss crag and one-storey wooden nest under peak is a rejected fear-driven fantasy, not visited geography. Empty garret's mood changes next morning.

places: Vane house; Lawn; Breakfast room; Garden porch
note: Rain on lawn, thrush/snail, rapid thunderstorm. Ground-floor window entry; Raven goes through little door to grass patch in nook between two wings of rambling house, via creeper-covered porch. Direct architectural relation; no exterior plan dimensions.
Raven claims rainy steppes of Uranus, all animals burrowers, emergent huge unfamiliar creatures and dry-bog-serpent. Remote world lore only, not on Vane's journey.

Stepping off porch onto wet grass while following Raven eventually reveals unfamiliar land. Worm becomes winged creature/cloud. Cemetery mentioned as Raven's workplace without location. No visible discrete portal on garden crossing.

places: Pine forest; Vane house; Seven dimensions
note: Entire surroundings are pine forest; Raven says Vane and house have not left one another and names region of seven dimensions. Large tree to left about thirty yards away is an explicit local measurement.

Raven locates tree on kitchen hearth, growing almost straight up chimney; reaching it crosses breakfast-room pianist. Rosebush beside woman; wild hyacinths inside piano strings. Objects/worlds occupy same place; smell/musical cross-sense experience. These claims do not yield normal planar overlay dimensions.
Appointment already broken days ago despite apparent short earthly interval; return through oneself, clock not governing this world. Raven leads toward wife. No cardinal route specified.

places: Pine forest; Open heath; Old church; Home-farm
note: Deeper forest has progressively larger, older, individually grotesque trees, then thins onto open heath. Ancient flowering hawthorn appears as white-headed man; Raven says it stands in earthly home-farm church ruins. Planned rose wilderness and three-yard no-plough buffer are Vane's intended improvements, not existing garden.
Faint windlike music; Raven says former worshippers still gather at ruins to sing. Ascending white pigeon is interpreted as prayer; sky/ethereal stair imagery, not a literal surveyed staircase.
Block of granite with unique anemone-like pale rose flower, golden centre and unfamiliar scent at its foot; prayer-flower explanation qualifies flora as spiritual manifestation.

Traverse rocky moor dry plants/mosses to cottage first visible at farthest distance. Gray-clouded descending sun, west sunset, abnormally cold wind. Flat unenclosed heath everywhere is cemetery, no church/graves visible, gray starless horizon only apparent wall. Day contains seasonal cycle: spring dawn, summer noon, autumn afternoon, winter night. Travel duration half-day seeming unreliable. Paradise/Noah's raven is comparison/remote lore.
Candle on central deal table; apparent coffin lid against wall opens as inner door; Eve stands before it. Character's eyes described as night-heaven are metaphor, not geographical heavens.
Raven remains earthly librarian and is librarian/sexton here; library-catacomb metaphor should not create another mapped catacomb. Multiple creature/tree/crystal selves described.

Wall cupboard holds bread/wine. Black kitten of Mara arrives and Eve takes it outside. House cannot serve as overnight halfway hostelry; sleepers cannot wake themselves. Candle-led passage through inner coffin-like door into great chamber.

Ice-house air through inner threshold; faint candle glints, innumerable couches in aisles, heads toward passage, white sheets. Moon through wall openings; uncertain whole shape alternates impression cathedral nave/huge barn. Bluish icy moonlight; isolated sleepers, adults and children but no infant seen. Three empty couches beside woman with wounded hand and middle-aged man; identities established later.

One of multiple treasure vaults; many sleepers lie on exterior moor thick as petals/leaves. Moon embalms here, unlike Earth's; few buried beneath ground. Cock on spire and resurrection bell mentioned by sexton, location/appearance not directly inspected. Vane's designated couch among three.
Cold heals sleepers' wounds; air pure/sweet until Vane brings death-odour. Rejected proposal to sleep outside because dead are there also. Vallombrosa is literary simile, not itinerary.

places: House of sleep; Library; Book closet
note: Escape through lengthy aisles and silent closing door into pitch darkness; next door opens directly into earthly library with masked-door handle in hand. Morning closet does not visibly reveal chamber. Small east-facing library window sends early sun via mirror to masked door; couch used overnight.
Reversed book's gilded edges reflect light to nest of drawers in dark closet corner; father's manuscript found. Reading position in western library window provides east/west architectural relation.
Father's manuscript opens with golden sun, blue sea and growing/flying things; no named coast or proof the estate adjoins this sea. Library encounter near ancestral portrait.

places: Book closet; Great hall; Lost tower; Other world
note: Sir Upward's original hundred-manuscript closet library. Historical route across great hall, steep rough descent, underground passage, newly built tower containing stair and top room with huge lock/tiny key. Crossing threshold reveals immense receding space and blue mountains under paler blue sky. Tower later disappeared. Raven uses house bottom-to-top route; world's physical/mental laws differ, moral laws shared. Account nested within father's manuscript; tower not present-day mapped building.
Door in/out and book/heart/world metaphors; more worlds and doors than narrator imagines. Not every figurative door is a literal geographical portal.

Father's ascent: light through edges of great roof slabs, floorless sections require stepping joist-to-joist. Partition rises amid one gap, chamber narrows upward through roof. Dusty floor-standing oblong mirror leaning against wall with eagle; opposite wall mirror. Chains rotate chamber top and alter sunlight at noon. Reflected rays pass through floor mirror; mist clears to mountain range and wide heath with retreating Raven. Mechanism is explicit; exact optics not established.

Father's death inference initially conjectural. After library sleep Vane ascends; adjusts hood and mirrors near noon. First vision tremulous and impermeable, later steady blue mountains; steps through into heather. Polarisation is Vane's hypothesis, not confirmed mechanism.

places: Heath; Thickets; Fir woods; Sexton's cottage
note: Search goes through many thickets and several small fir woods but does not locate expected pine forest. Near-horizon sun brings winter cold. Cottage route cannot be retraced simply from memory; Raven refuses to lead him this time. Last night versus last week discrepancy; daisies/roots of heaven reference sleepers.

Raven identifies sleeping man as Vane's father, others ancestors. Grandfather still fighting in Evil Wood where unwilling sleepers wake nightly to kill/bury their dead. Raven provides no precise wood location, says Vane will hardly miss it.

Many home routes; home in palm of hand language is spiritual, not a measured destination. Raven points toward beings like Vane: pointing direction contains blinding setting sun, supporting westward initial heading. Yellow luminous creature emerges as sun sets and Vane follows. Narrator again warns scenes may also be metaphysical arguments and descriptions cannot convey complete reality.

Light creature guides over rocky ground/heather, turns to dead book when grasped. Bitter winter night, full unfamiliar moon rising over level horizon. Nearby low hill range westward of moon becomes target; this is a relative bearing, not proof of Earth's lunar directions.

Heather gives way to bare spongy soil like dry powdery peat. Rippling/heaving earth inhabited by burrowing predatory monsters, tiger-like beast, red-necked polar-bear-headed worm with white mane, feathered serpent and other no-two-alike forms. Moonlight inhibits/paralyses them; retrospective knowledge, not initially understood. Sea/waters language here is metaphor for restless earth, not actual sea.

Near hills at moonset burrow initially quiet, mist-clad woman disintegrates into serpents/bat and ground heaves. Slope and summit cast shadow removing protection; pursuit toward still-moonlit ridge, rock shadow perilous. Creatures become blotches when entering moonlight. Hills delimit safe escape, not mileage.
Ridge top pure strong air, moon descends to low distant horizon. Short descent warmer; seated waiting dawn; darkness after moonset. No shelter structure specified.

places: Low hills; First dry river-bed; Evil Wood approach
note: Sunrise return to ridge shows apparently lifeless hollow behind. Ahead wide deserted land with distant differently coloured possible forest, no habitation/cultivation/cloud/haze. Descent reaches vast exposed rock river-bed, flat/channelled or humped/pinnacled, innumerable dry water-runs, dry moss and hard lichens. Whole day to forest; no water crossed. Audible water is aural mirage, not observed stream.

Enter before sunset; diverse familiar/unfamiliar tree species, not pine wood. Eucalyptus-like high smooth stem, low enclosing boughs, falchion leaves, skull-like lidded calyces and frothy bloom. Glades/aisles appear to close at night; abrupt cold. Foliage suggests wolves, horses, skeletons and woman as wind rises. Door/window language describes forest apertures, not houses.

Nocturnal commotion on all sides, moon reveals skeleton/phantom battle and misty or bone-white horses. Mistress with dark side-spot seen above battle. At pre-sunrise voice they collapse and no bones remain, only some withered branches. Daytime wood quiet without seen birds/small mammals/moths; faint burial noises. These temporal states belong to one wood.

Emerges mid-afternoon into second network of dry courses. Initially fears reverse heading; concludes another branch of same river, explicitly his inference. Sunset in broad channel, moss sleeping spot; water sounds when head touches ground. Dawn shadows stripe wrinkled rocks. 'North-west and by south' is paradoxical expression of uncertainty, not reliable compass bearing.

places: Second dry river-bed; Little Ones' hollow
note: Channel vegetation increases shrub-like plants to dwarf fruit trees then clumps filling channels. Larger coarse-fruited trees at rim of former lake basin; forest from left flows into hollow; valley trees mostly fruit-bearing. Grass/moss descending slope; cherry-sized rosy apples on tiny tree. Former lake interpretation made by narrator, not named lake.

Children throughout slope, some older in separate knot. Large green apple coarse/unpalatable compared with small fruits. Giant approaches from brow; Vane ascends to more level footing before ambush. Relative local elevation explicit.

Dragged to wood above valley: wretched huts of fallen branches and few stones; woman inside. Giants eat tubers, bulbs, coarse fruits. Next morning captive tied by long rope to valley tree and scrapes bark from fruitless branches with serrated flat stone; nourishing dwarf tree close by.

Tiny trees fill intervals like brushwood between big trees; many children hidden there. Giants almost blind to them, danger from stumpy feet. Captive nights on bare ground at hut door, children nest around him providing warmth against nightly cold. Lona comes out of wood carrying newborn; girls nurture younger children.

places: Little Ones' wood; Little Ones' hollow
note: Babies found through night searching in wood; source unexplained and some think dropped from trees. Small plums squeezed for baby sustenance. Lona says all have lived here always, no counting or ordinary age, fears growth into giants. Preserve epistemic limits: children know where found, not mechanism of origin.

places: Little Ones' hollow; Giants' settlement; Dry world
note: Vane notes no falling/lying/running water anywhere in other world so far; abundant ancient water evident. Children have never seen water before his tears; brook comparison is narrator's simile. Giants have no babies; children becoming greedy/lazy/big/stupid/bad leave Little Ones and lose identity. Small berries versus large green apples recur as ecological/moral divide.

Growth into giants erases recognition and affection; apple consumption expresses chosen character. Children cannot define 'world' as narrator does. Social/ecological transformation, not travel to separate continent.

Tolma found under beech tree. Largest fattest unseen giant worshipped in one of giants' houses, reported by Lona rather than visited. Blunty appears giant beside quince tree after vanishing. Beech/quince are explicit flora, unlike unspecified extra fantasy vegetation.

Long stay without desire to travel, then need to learn world and children. Attack beside work tree; evening stars expect moon. Water heard with ear against earth but never seen; fruit relieves thirst. Lava image is simile, not volcano.
Giants threaten injured Vane; children escort him slowly up slope with food and assistance. Moon just rises when procession reaches valley rim. Departure is night, not daytime.

Children know unnamed great place with giant-girl queen but cannot give distance/direction/name. Smooth green rockless/treeless country lies beyond baby-forest away where moon comes from. Their description is limited knowledge, later Mara supplies Bulika name.

Escort travels up second river-bed branch; stop when moon at height, farthest children have yet gone from trees. Warning of ugly scratching desert Cat-woman contradicted by Lona's reassurance. Vane continues alone after children retrace route.

Children's attachment to their country feels essential to identity; rejected suggestion to emigrate. Vane questions whether interventions would distort their nature; no literal boundary or national name established.

Full moon habitual so far; cottage silhouette in setting disc with light through open door/window. Closely successive small ravines block night progress; sleeps in sandy hollow, unfamiliar constellations. Mara protects from roaming night creatures; says house shadow would hide him but both doors open. Moon alignment is observed sightline, not location on lunar surface.

places: Mara's cottage; Lovers' country; Bags' settlement
note: Cottage poor, Mara lives alone except guests. She names giants Bags, Little Ones Lovers; neither knows own name. Leave channels and walk long time before cottage appears; walking elapsed time not quantifiable scale.

places: Bulika; Grassy country; Land of Waters; Little Ones' lake basin
note: Mara locates Bulika in smooth grassy country. Princess came from Vane's world and older than this world; transformed farming/shepherd community through diamond/opal mining and trade into city. Former country called Land of Waters: dry channels once live torrents, fruit valley former receiving lake. Princess removed at most half the waters in egg; remainder fled underground; subterranean waters sustain life. Mara's historical testimony, not direct observed ancient map. Palace library reportedly holds unreadable prophecy poem.

Thirst then water then growth; water still flows below. Vane confirms hearing healing water twice. No visible underground course mapped; Mara's rain/spring explanation is the book's world lore, not ordinary hydrology imposed on it.

Wide sand tract, rock foundation buried deep in sand; cottage resembles sexton's but thicker walls. Strong heavy door directly into large bare room, two small opposed glassless windows, two doors permitting moon sightline, hearth horn lantern. Narrow steep stair straight to unceiled/unpartitioned garret, one wide low dormer, narrow bed under sloping roof with white coverlet, table dry loaf and cold water. First actual drink of water in other world; this private provision qualifies general dryness, not evidence of nearby open river. Fruit-only stay has lasted months according to Vane.

places: Mara's cottage; Astarte's route; Other world's sky
note: Howling/purring at dormer; white woman strokes white panther-like animal by door and indicates horizon below moon halfway up sky; animal races on line. Moon had set a few hours before. Narrator later learns several moons serve world, never discovers periods/orbits. Compass from moon cannot be assumed terrestrial.

places: Mara's cottage; River-bed bank; Guide forest; Running-stream crossing; Bulika
note: Exact directions: go UP bank until bed disappears; verge RIGHT to forest; may stay night, leave facing rising moon; maintain heading to running stream; cross it at RIGHT ANGLES; straight until city on horizon. Astarte goes shortest way to Bulika, not necessarily same route as Vane. Forest here not automatically Evil Wood or baby-forest; later route evidence must identify it.

Mara says no one sleeps here two successive nights and predicts later long unwilling stay. Leaving/calling back abruptly reveals doorless house despite earlier two doors; circles house no entry. Gray cat springs from window and speeds toward river-bed; Vane falls face down in sand hearing sobs. Door change observed, not mundane missing-door omission.

places: Desert; Cataract scaur; Dry river branches; Evil Wood
note: Many unspecified desert miles; rocky ascent reached about sunset, green moss at base and third underground-water hearing. Scaur inferred former cataract head of channels. Sunrise summit reveals finest sand filling upper river course to plain. Looking back sees river divided into TWO branches as it fell: current followed bank and first crossed before Evil Wood. Evil Wood visible on far horizon BETWEEN branches. Desert ahead and left beyond sight; lift of forest skyline far RIGHT. This is strongest explicit landscape topology so far.

places: Guide forest; Baby-forest extension; Rose wood
note: Bread hardens to stone. About noon tamarisk/juniper, then stunted firs, larger firs/thickets, forest of pines/other trees resembling baby forest; same forest farther portion is Vane's belief. Large trees in nearly geometrical spacing, little undergrowth, long sightlines, distant moving things, some birds, many brilliantly coloured or white butterflies. Pines widen to flowering shrubs then tree-sized splendid roses, other species, immense columnar trunks.

Indeterminate house/castle shape with no verifiable masonry; apparent ivy-absorbed ruin is conjecture. Rectangular doorless gap enters hall-like open space: grass/flower floor, ivy/vine/rose walls and roof. Withered-leaf bed in corner, red sunset, warm night, branching ceiling with sky patches. Red roses disappear first in twilight, yellow/white later; stars through leaves. Numerous nesting birds, owl hunting mice. Aladdin's cave is simile, not another site.

Midnight apparent splendid hall with anciently dressed dancers, skull faces/living eyes. Moon through countless-windowed vegetal roof; bodies pass through Vane. Lilith-like woman dark side-mark appears doorway. Warm wind extinguishes lights, strips dancers to skeletons, eyes vanish; remains foliage/leaf motion and owl. Night manifestation of same hall; no separate ballroom destination.
Leaves hall into wood to resume journey; another moon rising, sets face toward it per Mara directions. Do not assume one Earth-like moon or time cycle.

Before walking ten paces after leaving the hall Vane sees the carriage, then approaches it; full separation is unmeasured. Ancient mouldering carriage upright on heavy wheels, fallen doors, two horse skeletons beside pole, coachman's skeleton on tattered hammer-cloth, two seated skeleton occupants. Local relic near hall, not known road or carriage route.

Skeleton movements around carriage, fibrous grass used to tie joint, fallen branch in bush used as crutch. Woodland said to extend enough for attempted separation. Hell/marriage language belongs to characters' interpretation, not established separate geographical region.

places: Skeleton carriage; Vegetal hall; Guide forest
note: Characters cannot get far apart or see others like themselves. Raven appears on beech bough directly overhead; hall explicitly close by and its dancers centuries spiritually in advance though physically adjacent. Vane/Raven not in hell while skeletons are: co-located spiritual states do not define ordinary bordered province.
Warning never obey/trust one who has deceived once. Raven appears several yards away flying low/fast; no mapped destination or reliable bearing.

Continue facing low rising copper-dark dented moon amid bright stars. Under spreading tree cold wasted woman on root-interlaced hard ground/pine needles. Ripe grapes gathered from forest-hall doorway; branch/leaf bedding made. Her original life/death and arrival explanations are conjectural.

places: Animal tracks; Guide forest edge; Hot river; Grassy plain
note: Before dawn eastern horizon clearer. Snake, doe/calf, bear-like cubs, miniature full-grown horses of many breeds, dwarf cattle and small elephants follow converging tracks. Well-beaten main track widens with tributary paths. Trees retreat and grass thickens to vast green horizon plain. Small brim-full deep river along forest EDGE, only few yards wide, bluish rising mist, hot metallic-tasting water; animals swim to grass and apparently sleep in wood. Animal habitat interpretation belongs to Vane.

places: Hot river; Spring hills; Hot-stream cave
note: Woman bathed in swift steady stream. Dry warm grass/soil. Vane follows river UP toward nearby rocky hills; river issues from rock at hill bottom. Initial imagined internal waterfall/stair disproved by inspection: water rises quietly from ground at BACK of little cave like column base, then along ONE SIDE in deep narrow channel, exit not wholly water-filled. No headwater cataract inside.

Boulders arranged around feet/sides. Fallen beech boughs with dry yellow leaves span stream to make bridge-bed; crossed branches/twigs packed with leaves/dry moss, warmth below. Repeated journeys to wood; seven days initially, longer stay follows. Baths nourish Vane like food/drink; grapes/berries from forest. A temporary artificial bridge-bed, not masonry bridge or established crossing.
Repeated dream of wounded angel is emotional dream, not new location or actual flying inhabitant. Account emphasises solitude and need for fellowship; no additional geography.

Cave stone searches fail; warm running water keeps air fresh yet sometimes oppressive, outdoor air cooler. Several weeks followed by additional week and regular night bites. Prickly-pear-like fibrous leaf skeletons, aloe-leaf stiletto and plant filaments used to sew clothing. Resemblance is stated; exact botanical identification not guaranteed.
Leaf-fibre sandals, couch of leaves. Woman claims six-foot white leech attacked, she threw it into river with audible splash. Treat as her possibly deceptive account, not confirmed animal species.

Awakening outside near cave; Vane tells discovery was in forest, not cave. Care lasted MORE THAN THREE MONTHS; flowing water carried hair in daily baths. Woman's repelling clenched left hand knocks Vane unconscious; wakes wet/shivering on ground. Sunup setting and near stream established, no journey away yet.

Woman moves swiftly AWAY from river across grass and up gentle slope; Vane bathes then follows/overtakes within three yards near noon. Distance unmeasured, no city yet visible. Sensation of night/stars while actual noon is emotional imagery.

Whole day walking thick soft grass until sunset exhaustion. Low moon's light gathered around woman. She speaks of gates of her city; at this point no gate reached. Repeated unconsciousness followed by unexplained cold/wet state, not proven stream crossing.

Woman sheds clothes/falls; spotted white long-bodied beast departs, pure white beast passes from behind and pursues SAME line into distance. Vane later follows this trail. Heard city slaughter is apparent/fancied distant outcry, not personally inspected attack scene. First transformation is inferred from disappearance; second pursuer distinct.

Mother runs with child on parallel line; Vane enters her track, attacking beast vaults over him. Spotted white leopardess returns slowly lame LEFT forepaw raised, copious flow mistaken for blood sounds like water over grass. Mother struck foot with stone. Small local scene without cardinal bearings.

Mother says fled Bulika, destination deliberately undisclosed. Reports princess sends spotted leopardess to kill babies, watches house doors, uses witches, alleged league with Shadows; admits knowledge of only one of purported two cats. Baby-prophecy reason for cruelty. No secret nursery location yet supplied.
Mother warns of night sounds like dead unable to shriek in palace; walks off on grass. Palace acoustic claim reported, not additional haunted site.

Lame beast's supposed blood is tested and found WATER: softly murmuring stream running over grass WITHOUT channel, enough force at ankles. Follows sound upstream toward city. At dawn wall-towers silhouetted in pale aurora; rivulet ends short of city leaving bent grass and small pools, none ahead. Temporary water trail, not a permanent river.

places: Bulika gardens; Walls; Gates; Refuse belt
note: Vegetable gardens close around walls, almost all unfamiliar plants, no flowers/water/animals seen. Huge gravel/refuse heaps thrown from battlements separate gardens from wall. Nearest gate half-closed, unsecured, unguarded, hinges apparently immovable. Long old silent street inside. Vane exits and walks long way across heaps and several radial roads leading to different gates.

places: Bulika streets; Bat-pillar square; Exterior grass
note: Next gate opens to narrow street of tall houses, little square with pillar bearing hideous bat-like figure. Further narrow streets; no children. Gate-near mob chases Vane, stops at walls; he sleeps a FEW HUNDRED YARDS outside in sunny grass. Gate count/plan unspecified, no surveyed grid.

places: Bulika streets; Narrow lane; Shadow's path
note: Night wake under familiar-seeming moon, evil-smelling cold wind from gate. Re-entry to long narrow street; white creature crosses; almost impassable lane connects to wider street. Shadow and white leopardess on opposite side, shadow cast by beast but Shadow itself flat two-dimensional opaque being. Flat paving stones. Wind through Shadow's glance causes shudder. Do not turn capitalised Shadow into terrain shadow alone.

Small archway off moonlit alley offers hiding place while spotted leopardess passes. Woman fears it watching her house door, reports cage/muzzle/crocodile-leather mitts/chains yet frequent escapes. Bitter wind; promise of indoor refuge. Reported restraints later observed in palace.

People dig precious stones in cellars, all manufactures made in OTHER TOWNS (unnamed/unlocated); inherited wealth/gem trade, work shunned. Strangers considered defiling and expelled before night; hypothetical guest-house would be demolished, not an actual inn. Princess allegedly power over air/water/earth and perhaps fire; citizen testimony biased. Hypothetical foreign invasion is not actual route.

Maze of lanes/passages to wider street. Narrow steep stair between two tall houses; top landing about man-length between opposite doors. Woman shuts own door on Vane, he lies on sheltered landing. No street name or side orientation.

places: Citizen's house; Stair landing; Interior passage
note: Moonlit street below, wind excluded from landing. Spotless white leopardess cannot turn on stair, somersaults out. Mara admits Vane into empty stone-paved chamber, rug floor bed, only moonlit ambient light. Adjacent room off narrow passage has newborn; white cat carries infant then Mara intervenes. Exterior stair route retraced; Vane initially misjudges rescuer cat as hostile.

Woman's pulped body falls into street few yards away; thrown from neighbouring window is Vane's inference. Shadow and spotless cat on opposite side; cat repels Vane pursuing them. No confirmed building height/throwing agent.

Palace seen earlier from square high ABOVE CITY HEART, many defences, fortress-like. Fortifications/city partly ruined/neglected. Huge strong gates open, drawbridge-like crossing over rocky chasm/ravine moat; Vane doubts it ever held water. Walls have small recessed stone bench used overnight; cold wind, silent moonlit structure, warming white cat. Imagined home garden scents on waking are mistaken, not portal return.

Circuit back to gates, crosses ravine moat to paved court with regularly spaced towering poplar-LIKE trees and taller central near-top-spreading palm-like tree. Palace style unfamiliar, suggesting Indian origin only to Vane: long LOW body, lofty CORNER towers, huge CENTRAL dome HALF tower height; central front low half-ellipse arch. Longish elliptical entrance hall, cage to one side with restrained spotted leopardess. TWO low passages branch into many narrow irregular ones; precise overall plan absent.

Large busy but listless-servant kitchen via page-led passages; spotless white cat accompanies. Further many passages reach enormous dark chamber: close-fitting BLACK MARBLE floor/wall, elliptical wall/plan, roof LONG HALF OF ELLIPSOID, high OVAL opening OVER ONE FOCUS of floor ellipse; only small light spot, wall absorbs light. Apparent reddish lines fleeting. Distinguish dome exterior from this interior roof: identity not explicitly established.

places: Black-marble chamber; White stair; Guest chamber
note: Princess appears in darkness/light spot; cold room. Many steps to BLACK CURTAIN; behind it WHITE STAIR up to beautiful guest room. Bath in corner, robe at couch foot; downstairs room to LEFT at stair foot. Vane says first roof since other city lodging, not proof of large travel gaps.

Great clear-water white bath SUNK in MARBLE floor, unusual delicate smell; Vane suspects enchantment/source but unproven. Downstairs LEFT room round, all ALABASTER, no windows, light filters through everywhere, low dome with flitting shadows. Ivory table/cakes/fruit/milk/wine/loaf, couch, silver goblets. Hybla and Hymettus are wine-flower comparisons, not world locations. Pitcher-plant is water analogy, not observed local flora.

places: Princess's claimed dominions; Hot river; Guide forest
note: Lilith claims millennia, imperial reach over savage dwarf-people, crossing hot river spell cast by another woman leading to collapse in forest. Dwarf savagery framing and leech rescue are deceptive testimony; do not map political borders or accept fauna/history solely from her. Step across river and route from city toward children may contain truthful details, needs Adam's later corroboration.
Clumsy glove on left fist; fearful roar makes alabaster tremble. Princess leads back up white stair to guest chamber; sound's animal source disputed by Vane and princess, not a geological earthquake.

Vane infers bounding river cancelled Lilith's leopard enchantment and she was en route to harm children; later Adam corroborates river safeguard. Ceiling-suspended lamp observed on waking; twilight sea is drugged sensation, not actual ocean.

places: Guest chamber; White stair; Alabaster room; Black hall
note: Tail disappears half-open room door; pursuit down stair to alabaster hall luminous under high moon. Pitch-dark corridor beyond, curtain into black hall. Independent shadows, dancers, mounted skeletons and burrow-beasts apparently mingle; boundaries unseen; hand-following wall reaches curtained vestibule opening. 'Secret cavern of sleep' is imagined threat, not actual mapped chamber.

places: Vestibule cage; Courtyard; Palace gate; Bulika
note: Silent human/beast struggle at cage; leopardess appears both leaving and still lying caged. Shadow crosses courtyard trees to gate, cat follows, then descent to city: palace elevation relative to city explicit. Half-high moon while earlier 'high' is approximate narration, not astronomical survey.

places: Citizen's stair; Bulika street; City gate
note: Shadow goes straight to previous lodging stair. Recognisable woman's crushed blackened body falls, spotted cat with baby descends. White cat attacks on paved street, Lilith transformation directly witnessed, wounded Lilith flees, white rescuer carries baby toward gate. Larger spotted versus smaller enduring white cat stated.

places: Palace hill; Vestibule; Black hall; Replayed landscapes
